title: 2027 Indiana Election Calendar (brochure)
notes: Text extracted 2026-11-09 (copy in sources/elections-run/). "This brochure reflects Indiana law as of August 2026." Jan 6, 2027 first day for major-party declarations for the municipal primary and for independent/minor-party petitions; noon Feb 5, 2027 declaration deadline; noon Feb 12 withdrawal; pre-primary campaign finance period ends April 9, report due noon April 16; primary May 4; petitions to the county voter registration office by noon June 30; consent and certified petition by noon July 15; pre-election period ends Oct 8, report due noon Oct 15; municipal election Nov 2, 2027; annual reports due noon Jan 20, 2027 (for 2026) and Jan 19, 2028 (for 2027).

title: 2026 Indiana Candidate Guide
notes: Text extracted 2026-11-09 (copy in sources/elections-run/). p. 3 and 11: primary candidates qualify by the party of their two most recent Indiana primary ballots or by a county chair's certification (IC 3-8-2-7); p. 11-12: Democratic precinct committeemen on the 2026 primary ballot, Republican in 2028; p. 20-21: city, county, township, town, school board and party-office declarations are filed with the county election board, CAN-42 is the municipal-year declaration; p. 35-36: local and school board candidates file campaign finance reports with the county election board, precinct committeemen file none; p. 104-105: school board petition (CAN-34) May 19 to noon June 18, 2026, 10 signatures in metropolitan and community corporations, South Bend (IC 20-23-15) and Mishawaka (IC 20-23-17) boards set by their own statutes, party label needs the two-primary history or a county chair's certification; p. 133: precinct committeemen file CAN-37 and no CAN-12.

title: 2026 Indiana Campaign Finance Manual (revised July 2026)
notes: Text extracted 2026-11-09 (copy in sources/elections-run/). p. 9-10: CFA-1 statement of organization due by noon 10 days after becoming a candidate or noon 7 days after the filing deadline, whichever is first (IC 3-9-1-5); offices paying under $5,000 a year and school board offices need a committee only after more than $500 raised or spent (IC 3-9-1-5.5); precinct committeeman candidates need no committee; p. 13: in municipal years city and town candidates file the pre-primary and pre-election reports even without a contested election (IC 3-9-5-9(d)).

title: IC 3-10-1-4.5 and 3-10-1-4.6 (years precinct committeemen are elected)
notes: Read 2026-11-09 (FindLaw "Current as of January 01, 2026"). Sec. 4.5(a): "Except as provided in section 4.6", May 2026, 2030, 2034 and every four years; sec. 4.6: "applies to precinct committeemen elected by the Indiana Republican Party", May 2024, 2028, 2032 and every four years.

title: IC 3-8-2-7 (declaration of candidacy; party affiliation test)
notes: Read 2026-11-09 (FindLaw "Current as of January 01, 2026"). Sec. 7(a)(4): affiliated only if (A) the two most recent Indiana primaries in which the candidate voted were that party's (a nonpartisan ballot in either requires the chair's certification) or (B) the county chairman of that party certifies the candidate is a member.
